latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 8401Q
Distil PLC
17 August 2026
Distil Plc
17 August 2026
Board changes - update
Distil Plc (AIM:DIS), confirms that, further to the notification of 15 July 2026, David Smith has today joined the board as Chief Executive Officer, completing the board changes announced by the Company on 15 July 2026
David has over 25 years of drinks experience working for IDV, Diageo, the West Indies Rum Distillery and most recently The Oxford Artisan Distillery. David was initially Executive Chairman and then CEO of Fielden Whisky over a 5-year period, transforming it from a founder-led artisanal distillery to a purpose-led business. Securing two rounds of angel investor funding and then in November 2022, merging the distillery with its grain supply partner to create an entity which secured investment from Diageo via its Distill Ventures investment vehicle.
He drove significant growth at Diageo via Smirnoff Mule, one of the forerunners of the RTD (ready-to-drink) cocktail business, and as Regional Director North America for Malibu. David has also built brands in export markets at the West Indies Rum Distillery and been involved in the 0% ABV category, launching and building new brands in the UK market.
Philip Naughton, Non-Executive Chairman of Distil, commented:
"David brings extensive experience of the premium drinks industry. I'm delighted to welcome him and I look forward to working closely with him and the wider team to deliver the Company's next phase of growth."
David Smith, CEO of Distil, commented:
"I have always been very impressed by Distil's levels of innovation and the quality of its products. I'm very excited to meet the team and build on the great platform that Don and they have created and to take the business on the next stage of its journey."

latest.content:
Today 07:00

DISTIL PLC
("
Distil

Company

U.S. order for Blavod
Distil Plc (AIM: DIS), owner of premium drinks brands including RedLeg Spiced Rum, Blackwoods Gin and Vodka, and Blavod Black Vodka, is pleased to announce that it has received the first order through its U.S. distribution partner to bring Blavod Black Vodka back into the U.S. market.
Highlights:
·
Blavod previously experienced success in the U.S. market and benefits from latent brand awareness
·
Vodka is the largest spirits category by volume and value in the U.S.
o
The U.S. is one of the largest spirits markets by volume and value globally (IWSR).
·
Distil's new distribution partner boasts an extensive distribution network across the U.S., Canada and Puerto Rico, with strong retail relationships
·
First shipment is substantial and expected to leave the UK early in Q3 (of the current financial period ending 31 March 2027)
The Company engaged AIKO Importers, Inc. ("AIKO"), a recognised importer and brand builder of premium wine and spirits, as its U.S. distribution partner in April 2025. Progress was subsequently delayed by tariff uncertainty and by TTB (Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau) label and liquid approvals, which were held up in part by government shutdowns.
Vodka represents the biggest spirit category in the U.S. by volume and value, one of the biggest spirits markets globally based on 2024 and 2025 figures from IWSR Drinks Market Analysis. Leveraging AIKO's extensive distribution network of 185 partners across the U.S., Canada and Puerto Rico, as well as strong retail relationships with major accounts like Costco, Total Wine, and Spec's, Blavod will benefit from immediate reach.
Production to fulfil this order will be handled through Inter-Continental Brands Ltd (the production arm of Fortitude Spirits Group, Distil's new UK distributor), and it is expected that the shipment will leave the UK early in Q3. This will represent the first production run under the new agreement with Fortitude.
Don Goulding, Executive Chairman, Distil Plc, commented:
"We're delighted to have reached this stage with AIKO following a lengthy process that was beyond the control of both parties.
"Unlocking distribution for Blavod in the U.S. marks an important moment and a fresh growth opportunity for the brand which has previously enjoyed success in this market before its previous distributor pulled back during the Covid lockdowns.
"We regularly receive requests for the product from customers and consumers, demonstrating strong brand awareness and demand, and we look forward to working closely with the AIKO team to rebuild the brand in this market."
Feliks Shekhtman, Managing Partner of AIKO, commented:
"We're thrilled to now be able to work directly with Blavod to rebuild the brand. It aligns closely with our mission to deliver high-quality, culturally relevant products that resonate with today's consumers, and we believe it has strong potential in the U.S. market.
"At AIKO, we pride ourselves on helping brands scale through our national infrastructure, deep market knowledge, and strong retail partnerships. We've seen tremendous success with brands like Clap Back Wine and Doc
Holliday Bourbon, and we look forward to achieving similar growth and success with Blavod."
About Blavod
Blavod original black vodka is a dramatic and stylish vodka with a clean taste. For almost two decades the unique black vodka has been made to the original recipe using only natural ingredients. Black catechu, extracted from the acacia tree found in south-east Asia is subtly infused into triple distilled grain vodka to produce an elegantly black, smooth and clean tasting premium vodka.
About AIKO
AIKO Importers is a nationally recognised importer of premium alcoholic beverages with a proven track record of scaling standout brands like Doc Holliday Bourbon, Clap Back Wine, and HanJan. With distribution across the U.S., Puerto Rico and Canada, AIKO delivers reach through 185 distributor partners and strong retail relationships with major players including Costco, Total Wine, and Spec's. Backed by decades of market expertise and a dedicated sales force, AIKO is known for bringing quality, culturally relevant brands to shelves across North America.

Notice of AGM; Proposed Capital Reorganisation
Distil plc (AIM:DIS) announces
that its Annual General Meeting ("AGM") will be held at 10.00 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026 at the offices of Allenby Capital Limited, 5 St Helen's Place,
London, EC3A 6AB.
Distil further announces that the audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 ("Report & Accounts") is near completion but has yet to be finalised. The Company expects to publish its Report & Accounts before 30 September 2026.
The Notice of AGM and Form of Proxy will be posted to shareholders today. Copies of these documents will shortly be available on the Company's website at
www.distil.uk.com
Capital Reorganisation
Resolutions at the AGM include those to facilitate a capital reorganisation.
Pursuant to the provisions of section 580 of the Act, the Company may not issue shares at an issue price which is less than the nominal value of those shares. The market price for the Company's existing Ordinary Shares is currently below its nominal value.
In order to enable the Company to issue new Ordinary Shares at an issue price which exceeds their nominal value, while maintaining the same number of Ordinary Shares in issue, Shareholders' approval is being sought to undertake the Capital Reorganisation.
The Company is proposing the subdivision and re-designation of the existing Ordinary Shares and an amendment to the Company's articles of association, in order to achieve a reduction in the par value of each existing Ordinary Share.
The Company presently has 2,033,799,769 existing Ordinary Shares in issue, each of which has a nominal value of 0.1 pence.
It is proposed that each of the 2,033,799,769 existing Ordinary Shares will be subdivided into and redesignated as one new Ordinary Share of 0.01p and 1 B Deferred Share of 0.09p.
Existing share certificates will remain valid instruments of title - no replacement share certificates will be issued following the Capital Reorganisation.
CREST accounts of Shareholders will not be credited in respect of any entitlement to new B Deferred Shares, and no share certificates will be issued in respect of the new B Deferred Shares.

latest.title: Board Changes
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 3388M
Distil PLC
15 July 2026
Inside Information
This announcement contains inside information for the purposes of the UK Market Abuse Regulations ('UK MAR'). Upon publication of this announcement, this inside information (as defined in UK MAR) is now considered to be in the public domain. The person responsible for arranging the release of this announcement on behalf of the Company is Mr Don Goulding, Executive Chairman.
Distil plc (the "Company")
BOARD CHANGES
Distil plc (AIM: DIS), the owner of premium drinks brands RedLeg Spiced Rum, Blackwoods Gin and Vodka, and Blavod Black Vodka, is pleased to announce the following proposed Board changes as the Company positions itself for its next phase of growth.
Highlights
·
Don Goulding is retiring as Executive Chairman with effect from 14th August
·
Philip Naughton will assume the position of Non-Executive Chairman with effect from 14th August
·
David Smith will be appointed as CEO with effect from 17th August
·
The Company will also seek to bolster the Board with the appointment of an additional independent non-executive director
Retirement of Don Goulding as Executive Chairman
Don Goulding announces that he will step down from the Board of Distil on 14 August 2026. On his retirement, his position will be split, with Philip Naughton becoming Non-Executive Chairman from 14 August 2026, in addition to the appointment of a full-time CEO, detailed below.
Don is retiring from Distil to focus on existing family projects after 16 years with the Company. Having first joined the Board as a Non-Executive Director in 2010, he subsequently became Chairman before assuming the role of Executive Chairman.
During his tenure, Don has played a pivotal role in shaping Distil's strategy and development. He led the creation of RedLeg Spiced Rum, transforming it into one of the Company's flagship brands, successfully guided the business through the unprecedented challenges of the Covid-19 pandemic, spearheaded the Company's strategic investment in Ardgowan Distillery, and recently secured a significant new production and distribution partnership to support future growth in the UK and international markets.
Appointment of Philip Naughton as Chairman
Philip Naughton will assume the position of Non-Executive Chairman on 14 August 2026, having previously joined the Distil board in February 2026 as a non-executive director (announced 28 January 2026).
Philip has extensive corporate experience within the financial services industry, in particular specialising in compliance and governance. Philip was most recently the CEO of a consulting firm. Under his leadership that firm undertook two successful private equity funding rounds.
Proposed Appointment of David Smith as Chief Executive Officer
The Company is delighted to announce the proposed appointment of David Smith as Chief Executive Officer.
David has over 25 years of drinks experience working for IDV, Diageo, the West Indies Rum Distillery and most recently The Oxford Artisan Distillery. David was initially Executive Chairman and then CEO of Fielden Whisky over a 5 year period, transforming it from a founder-led artisanal distillery to a purpose-led business. Securing two rounds of angel investor funding and then in November 2022, merging the distillery with its grain supply partner to create an entity which secured investment from Diageo via its Distill Ventures investment vehicle.
At Diageo he assisted in the launch of RTDs (Ready to Drinks) and built brands in export markets at the West Indies Rum Distillery. David has also been involved in the 0% ABV category, launching and building new brands in the UK market.
It is proposed that Mr Smith will join the Board, subject to the successful completion of the Company's Nominated Adviser's customary due diligence process. A further announcement regarding Mr Smith's appointment will be made once the due diligence process has been completed.
Don Goulding commented:
"As the market begins to recover following a prolonged period of industry-wide challenges, and with a strong strategic production and distribution partner now in place across the UK and export markets, this is the right time for me to step aside.
The Company is well positioned for its next phase of development, and I am delighted that we are strengthening the leadership team by separating the Executive Chairman role and CEO roles. David brings industry experience and a strong track record of building premium drinks brands, while Philip has already made an excellent contribution since joining the Board earlier this year.
I leave knowing the business has a talented team, a strong portfolio of brands and significant opportunities ahead. I wish everyone at Distil every success for the future."
Philip Naughton commented:
"I have greatly enjoyed getting to know the team since joining the Board in February and am honoured to be taking on the role of Non-Executive Chairman at such an exciting point in the Company's development.
Don has provided exceptional leadership and stewardship over the past 16 years. In particular, over the last year he has successfully guided the Company through a number of significant challenges while laying the foundations for the next stage of growth. On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank him for his dedication, vision and commitment to Distil.
I am also delighted to welcome David Smith to the team. David brings extensive experience of the premium drinks industry, most recently the development and successful sale of the Fielden whisky brand. I look forward to working closely with David and the wider team as we build on Distil's strong foundations to support and deliver the Company's next phase of growth."
David Smith commented:
"I have been aware of Distil for many years and I've always been very impressed by their levels of innovation and the quality of their products. Their portfolio has wide consumer appeal and is positioned well for growth against the current trends around affordability. I'm very excited to build on the great platform that Don and the team have created and to take the business on the next stage of his journey"

company_30s.what_they_do: DIS.L is a small UK‑based specialty retailer that sells a range of niche consumer goods, including premium spirits, home décor, and boutique packaging solutions. The business is structured around a handful of private labels such as RedLeg, Blavod, and Blackwoods, which it markets through a network of independent distributors and its own online store.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company taps into the growing consumer appetite for boutique, artisanal products that command higher margins than mass‑market rivals. Its private‑label strategy gives it pricing flexibility and a direct relationship with customers, while the distribution partnership with Fortitude expands its reach into new UK regions.
company_30s.current_state: DIS.L is currently in a phase of restructuring. Recent board changes, a capital reorganisation, and the conversion of a convertible loan note signal a focus on stabilising cash flow and preparing for a potential sale of non‑core assets. The company is still trading at a very low price, reflecting a steep decline in market confidence.

rns_narrative: The company is busy shuffling its capital structure: an AGM notice, a capital reorganisation proposal, and a board reshuffle all point to a top‑down effort to reset governance and attract fresh capital.

Operationally, the focus has shifted to consolidating the brand portfolio—Ardgowan CLN conversion, the launch of RedLeg packaging refresh, and the US order for Blavod suggest a push to strengthen core product lines.
There is a clear theme of ‘stabilisation and positioning’: the company is trimming excess, tightening its balance sheet, and preparing to showcase a more coherent business model to investors.

crowd_tape.bull_narrative: No clear bullish chatter – the few posts that exist are generic product links and do not signal investor confidence.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the repeated restructuring announcements and the lack of any concrete growth story. The repeated mention of 'capital reorganisation' and 'holding(s) in company' fuels concerns about liquidity and potential dilution.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The conversation has gone from mild curiosity about new product launches to a flat, almost silent tone. The community is not rallying around any narrative, which is a classic sign that the market is waiting for a decisive catalyst.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is dead – no recent search activity. This silence means the market is not currently watching, leaving room for a surprise catalyst to generate a large move.

near_term_catalysts: A formal AGM that approves the proposed capital reorganisation – if the plan includes a new equity raise or a strategic partnership, it could inject fresh cash.
The completion of the Ardgowan CLN conversion – converting the debt into equity would improve the balance sheet and could trigger a positive narrative.
A press release announcing a new distribution agreement with a major retailer or a significant bulk order from the US for Blavod.
A spike in trading volume that exceeds the 30‑day average by 200% – a classic sign of institutional interest that could precede a bounce.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a clear break of the 20‑day moving average on higher volume, a sudden uptick in the number of institutional holdings, and any mention of a new product launch or partnership in the next earnings call.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of capitulation. The APEX score indicates a tight compression, suggesting that a small catalyst could push the price out of the current squeeze. If the price starts to move above the recent support level, it would signal the start of mean reversion.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company sits well below its historical lows – estimates suggest a 70‑90% drop from peak. Historically, a deep crash followed by a clean reorganisation often yields a 200‑300% rebound to the midpoint of the previous range. The recent restructuring and product refreshes provide a plausible path back to sustainable earnings.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still lacks a clear revenue driver – the latest news is all about balance‑sheet tweaks, not sales growth. If the capital reorganisation fails or if the company cannot secure a new distribution deal, the price could stay depressed and the stock might even be forced into a delisting scenario.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside of roughly 3× (recovering to the midpoint of the previous range) versus a downside limited to the current price (no further loss beyond the existing market cap). The risk/reward ratio is therefore about 3:1, favouring a contrarian stance.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price closes above the 20‑day moving average with volume at least 150% of the 30‑day average. Size the position so that a 10% drop would be the stop‑loss. Use a trailing stop that follows the price once it moves 5% higher.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until you see either a formal AGM approval of the capital plan or a sudden volume spike above 200% of the 30‑day average. If either occurs, consider a small position to test the waters.
playbook.if_passing: No terminal risk has been identified, so the setup is not a passing scenario. Continue to monitor for any signs of delisting or bankruptcy filings.

ai_insights.bottom_line: DIS.L is a deep‑crashed, low‑sentiment stock that has just begun a restructuring engine; a successful capital reorganisation could trigger a 3× rebound, making it a compelling contrarian play.
